definitions.explanation: A behavioral tendency, often unconscious; can refer to good or bad habits, but frequently implies a bad or unusual habit.
Natural wave or curl in hair.

examples.japanese: {悪|わる}い{癖|くせ}を{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my bad habit.
examples.notes: 癖を直す = to fix a habit

examples.japanese: {爪|つめ}を{噛|か}む{癖|くせ}がある。
examples.english: I have a habit of biting my nails.
examples.notes: 〜癖がある = to have a habit of ~

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{口癖|くちぐせ}は「まあ」だ。
examples.notes: 口癖 = verbal habit, pet phrase

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}からの{癖|くせ}で、{考|かんが}える{時|とき}に{頭|あたま}をかく。
examples.english: It's a habit from childhood — I scratch my head when I think.

examples.japanese: {一度|いちど}{癖|くせ}になると、なかなか{直|なお}らないものだ。
examples.english: Once something becomes a habit, it's quite hard to break.
examples.notes: 癖になる = to become a habit

examples.english: My hair has a natural wave.

examples.japanese: {癖|くせ}のある{髪|かみ}をまっすぐにしたい。
examples.english: I want to straighten my curly hair.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{髪|かみ}の{癖|くせ}が{強|つよ}くなる。
examples.english: On rainy days, the curl in my hair gets stronger.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}も{同|おな}じように{髪|かみ}に{癖|くせ}があるので、{遺伝|いでん}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: My mother has the same wavy hair, so I think it's genetic.

examples.japanese: {癖|くせ}の{強|つよ}い{髪|かみ}だが、{最近|さいきん}はそのままにしている。
examples.english: My hair has strong curls, but lately I've been leaving it as it is.

notes:
USAGE: {癖|くせ} often has a negative connotation, referring to bad habits or peculiar behaviors. However, it can also be neutral.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{癖|くせ}がある (to have a habit of)
・{癖|くせ}になる (to become a habit)
・{癖|くせ}を{直|なお}す (to fix a habit)
・{口癖|くちぐせ} (verbal habit, catchphrase)
・{悪|わる}い{癖|くせ} (bad habit)

GRAMMAR:
・〜{癖|くせ}に (despite ~, even though ~) - a conjunctive use expressing criticism

CONTRAST:
・{癖|くせ} - habit (often negative or quirky)
・{習慣|しゅうかん} - habit, custom (neutral, established routine)
